transcription.text: Higgsfield said they'd open sourced their platform.
We took them at their word and went one step further.
What if every video was its own source code?
This is Forkfield.
Pick an effect, add a photo,
and in about a minute you get a vertical clip with sound.
Portal to Mars, action figure, museum piece, outfit flip,
earth zoom out, comic panel,
six recipes to start.
On Higgsfield, the effect is the product,
and it stays locked inside their app.
In Forkfield, the recipe ships inside the MP4 itself.
See a clip you like?
Drop it in.
Forkfield reads the recipe right in your browser,
so the file never leaves your device.
Add your own photo, and you've forked it.
Change one line of the recipe,
and you've made a brand new effect.
Linked back to the one it came from.
Every fork lands in the fork tree.
Under the hood, it's one comfy UI graph, open weights only.
Quen image edit draws your final frame and keeps your face.
LTX 2.5 animates from your photo to that frame with audio.
On comfy cloud, a clip takes under a minute of GPU.
The graph rides inside the file too,
and the public demo runs on Cloudflare workers.
No preset store.
No gatekeeper.
The video is the preset.
Forkfield.
Fork any video.
MIT licensed.
On GitHub.
Now.
